submission.justification:
Absorber-F3 at 4 mm gives the best simulated 100 GeV electron resolution I found: 3.11%. Nearby points for F3 are 3.74% (2 mm), 3.28% (5 mm), 3.32% (6 mm) and 4.53% (10 mm), so 4 mm is the local optimum. Best results for the other materials were Absorber-F2 about 3.9% (3 mm, 5 mm) and Absorber-F1 about 5.2% (5 mm). The residual dose-rate constraint (<= 20 uSv/h at 1 m after one week of cooldown) could NOT be verified. None of the project documents give activation or dose data for any absorber, and the simulation tool only returns resolution. This is a hard requirement, so the recommendation is conditional: a dose/activation calculation for F3 (and for F2 as the fallback) must be completed before this choice is adopted. If F3 fails the dose limit, Absorber-F2 at about 3-5 mm is the next option on resolution, subject to the same check. Cooling (18 C water, electronics-dominated heat load), readout (common to all options) and mechanical support (compatible with all candidates) do not distinguish the materials.</justification>
